jobs.title: Director, Engineering and Research
jobs.description:
Job Description:

Rakuten Group, Inc.
(TSE: 4755) is a global technology leader in services that empower individuals, communities, businesses, and society. Founded in Tokyo in 1997 as an online marketplace, Rakuten has expanded to offer services in e-commerce, fintech, digital content and communications to 2 billion members around the world. The Rakuten Group has around 30,000 employees, and operations in 30 countries and regions. For more information visit https://global.rakuten.com/corp/.

Job Summary:

Rakuten Americas’ AI & Data Division (AIDD) is seeking a passionate and experienced Director, Engineering and Research to play a pivotal role in bridging cutting-edge research with robust engineering capabilities to solve critical business needs. AIDD’s mission is to build world-class AI experiences that serve as the digital core of Rakuten’s global ecosystem.

In this role, you will focus on AI applications such as agent experiences, search, recommendation, personalization, and the broader customer experience—delivering meaningful impact for nearly 2 billion Rakuten users. Inspired by our CEO’s vision, “No AI, No Rakuten,” you will help ensure AI is embedded at the heart of everything we do.

You will define and execute multi-year technical and research roadmaps that align foundational research with real-world engineering execution. You will lead interdisciplinary teams, scale operations, and oversee the full lifecycle of innovation—from early-stage prototypes to production-ready, large-scale systems. The role requires close collaboration with executive stakeholders across Research, Product, Business, and global Rakuten teams to drive integrated, high-impact AI initiatives.

Key Responsibilities:

Strategic Leadership & Interdisciplinary Vision

Define and drive multi-year technical and research roadmaps, ensuring seamless integration of scientific discovery with scalable engineering implementation.
Champion a culture of deep collaboration between research and engineering, breaking down silos to accelerate innovation and solution delivery.
Guide architectural direction, modern engineering practices, and the adoption of technologies emerging from internal and external research.
Provide expert leadership on the transition from research prototypes to reliable, secure, production-grade systems.
Establish cross-functional standards and processes that support both research excellence and engineering efficiency.

Organizational & People Management

Build, mentor, and scale high-performing interdisciplinary teams, including both ICs and managers.
Lead talent strategies—recruitment, retention, performance management, and career development—for a diverse, technically excellent organization.
Communicate vision, goals, and priorities across functions, ensuring strong alignment and shared ownership.
Optimize resource allocation across multiple product lines and initiatives, balancing delivery velocity with long-term innovation.
Accountable for resource planning and budgetary oversight.

Cross-functional Collaboration & Business Impact

Partner with executive stakeholders in Research, Product, Business, and Operations to align on technical direction and deliver integrated solutions.
Drive cross-functional initiatives by uniting research and engineering contributions toward shared business goals.
Serve as a technical and scientific ambassador internally and externally, representing the team’s innovation and capabilities.
Identify and support strategic partnerships and business development opportunities that leverage the team’s research-engineering synergy.

Qualifications

To perform this job successfully, an individual must demonstrate excellence across the following domains. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Exceptional leadership in defining, communicating, and executing multi-year technical and research roadmaps for complex, large-scale systems.
Proven track record of building, coaching, and scaling interdisciplinary engineering and research organizations that deliver innovative, research-informed software products.
Deep expertise in architecting and operating scalable, secure, and resilient cloud-native systems, combined with a strong foundation in research methodology and experimental design.
Mastery of the full software development lifecycle, modern DevOps practices, and a commitment to engineering quality and scientific rigor.
Demonstrated ability to align and influence executive stakeholders across Research, Product, Business, and Operations on strategic, cross-functional initiatives.
Strong technical acumen in AI/ML domains, including LLMs, NLP, search, recommendation systems, and conversational AI.
Comfortable leading through ambiguity in fast-moving, international environments, managing globally distributed teams.
Outstanding communication and interpersonal skills; ability to translate complex technical and scientific concepts across diverse stakeholders.
Proven ability to attract, develop, and retain top-tier engineering and research talent, fostering a culture of innovation, psychological safety, and continuous learning.
Experience or strong potential for engaging in strategic partnerships and business development initiatives.
Fluency in English is required; proficiency in Japanese is a plus.

Minimum Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field. Master’s or Ph.D. preferred. A Ph.D. in a relevant AI/ML research field (e.g., Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Statistics, Operations Research) is highly desirable.
12+ years of progressive experience in software engineering and/or applied research, including 5+ years in senior manager or director-level leadership roles.
Significant hands-on experience with large-scale, distributed systems and modern cloud platforms (e.g., AWS, GCP, Azure).
Proven ability to translate AI/ML research advancements—including Deep Learning, NLP, LLMs, and conversational AI—into scalable production systems.
Demonstrated success in leading large, interdisciplinary teams toward high-impact outcomes that combine research excellence with engineering precision.

Five Principles for Success

Our worldwide practices describe specific behaviors that make Rakuten unique and united across the world. We expect Rakuten employees to model these 5 Shugi Principles of Success.

Always improve, Always Advance
- Only be satisfied with complete success - Kaizen

Passionately Professional
- Take an uncompromising approach to your work and be determined to be the best

Hypothesize - Practice - Validate – Shikumika
- Use the Rakuten Cycle to succeed in unknown territory

Maximize Customer Satisfaction
- The greatest satisfaction for our teams is seeing their customers smile

Speed!! Speed!! Speed!!
- Always be conscious of time - take charge, set clear goals, and engage your team

We are the champions of childhood

Hanna Andersson is a Portland, Oregon-based premier kids and baby clothing brand . Our clothes are made to play, made to last, and designed to let kids be kids
. We have core commitments to design, quality, and sustainability,
and we believe in helping families create meaningful everyday moments.
These principles guide the Hanna Way, and lead to an experience authentically different from other children’s brands.

We cultivate our unique brand by hiring team members who believe in these values, own a customer service mindset, and who are innovative, results-oriented, and comfortable working in a collaborative and growth-driven work environment. We all share in our brand’s success, and we actively encourage our team members to maintain a healthy balance in their daily lives.

Position Summary

The Director of Ecommerce Engineering is a technology leader responsible for delivering secure, scalable, reliable, and high-performing digital commerce solutions that enable exceptional customer experiences and support Hanna Andersson's long-term growth.

Reporting to the Chief Technology Officer, this role leads the ecommerce engineering organization through people leadership, technical stewardship, operational excellence, and cross-functional partnership. The Director is accountable for building high-performing engineering teams, delivering strategic initiatives, modernizing the commerce platform, and ensuring technology investments align with business objectives.

The Director will lead the evolution of Hanna's commerce ecosystem - including Salesforce Commerce Cloud, headless commerce, payment platforms, customer data capabilities and CRM, AI-enabled engineering practices, OMS, product information mangement, POS, and future omnichannel initiatives - while driving continuous improvement in engineering quality, delivery, reliability, and operational efficiency.

This is a full-time, exempt position. The role may be remote or hybrid based on business needs and requires close collaboration with cross-functional teams. The Director is expected to support critical production events, peak business periods, and high-priority initiatives while fostering a culture of continuous improvement and operational excellence.

What You'll Do

Engineering Leadership & Organizational Health

Build, lead, coach, and retain a high-performing engineering organization of 1-4 scrum teams, through hiring, mentoring, performance management, career development, and contracting.
Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, innovation, quality of craft, continuous learning, and operational excellence.
Establish clear expectations, monitor organizational health, and ensure the team has the skills, capacity, and engagement necessary to meet business objectives.
Work closely with other IT leaders across Infrastructure, Data, Technical, Operations and Infosec to ensure platforms, integrations, and services meet enterprise standards for security, reliability, scalability, performance, and operational excellence.

Delivery Execution & Engineering Operations

Own delivery of the ecommerce engineering roadmap, ensuring predictable execution of strategic initiatives, releases, operational priorities, and production support.
Manage priorities, dependencies, risks, resourcing, and release readiness while improving delivery quality, transparency, and predictability.
Continuously improve engineering operating practices, including Agile delivery, SDLC, QA, DevOps, CI/CD, release management, incident response, and operational support.
Establish and monitor KPIs to assess team and stack performance and use data-driven insights to inform decisions.

Technical Leadership & Platform Stewardship

Provide technical leadership across ecommerce applications, integrations, architecture, and platform modernization initiatives.
Establish engineering standards that promote scalability, maintainability, extendability and performance.
Work with cross functional teams to build in security, accessibility, and reliability, and long-term platform health.
Champion the long-term health of Hanna’s ecommerce technology ecosystem by establishing technical direction, architecture, and governance that enable efficient sustainable growth and operational excellence.
Lead modernization of Hanna's commerce ecosystem, including Salesforce Commerce Cloud, composable commerce, APIs, integrations, cloud services, and supporting technologies.

Platform Reliability & Customer Experience

Ensure the availability, scalability, security, and performance of customer-facing ecommerce platforms.
Proactively prepare systems for seasonal peaks, product launches, and other high-volume events while minimizing operational risk and customer impact.
Partner across engineering, infrastructure, and security teams to continuously improve monitoring, resiliency, incident management, and operational maturity.

Cross-Functional Leadership

Partner with Program Management, Product, UX, Ecommerce, Marketing, Merchandising, Customer Experience, Operations, Distribution, Finance, and Information Systems to translate business strategy into technology execution.
Build trusted relationships across the organization, communicate technical tradeoffs clearly, and ensure engineering serves as a strategic business partner.
Drive alignment across stakeholders through effective planning, governance, communication, and transparent reporting.

Technology Strategy, Innovation & AI

Evaluate emerging technologies and identify opportunities to improve customer experience, engineering productivity, and business performance.
Champion responsible adoption of AI across engineering, leveraging modern tools to improve software development, testing, documentation, operational efficiency, and developer effectiveness while maintaining appropriate governance and quality standards.
Support the evolution of Hanna's digital capabilities, including personalization, search, fulfillment, customer data, and future omnichannel experiences.

Vendor, Financial & Platform Stewardship

Lead strategic relationships with technology vendors, implementation partners, and managed service providers.
Support platform selection, contract negotiations, renewals, budgeting, and technology investment decisions while optimizing cost, value, scalability, and long-term maintainability.
Ensure third-party partners meet delivery expectations, technical standards, security requirements, and service commitments.

Strategic Programs & Special Projects

Lead cross-functional strategic initiatives beyond day-to-day engineering operations, including platform modernization, enterprise integrations, organizational transformation, and executive-sponsored technology programs.
Partner across customer experience, brand marketing, payments, finance, operations, and fulfillment experience initiatives to deliver integrated business capabilities.

You Should Have

Required Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

Demonstrated success leading and developing high-performing software engineering organizations.
Extensive experience delivering customer-facing ecommerce platforms and digital commerce solutions.
Strong understanding of modern ecommerce architectures, including headless or composable commerce platforms, Salesforce Commerce Cloud, APIs, cloud technologies, integrations, and microservices.
Experience integrating ecommerce platforms with payment, merchandising, product and pricing/promotion systems, CRM, OMS, fulfillment, and customer engagement technologies.
Strong knowledge of Agile delivery, DevOps, CI/CD, software quality, observability, security, and engineering best practices.
Experience applying AI-enabled engineering tools and automation to improve software delivery, quality, and operational effectiveness.
Proven ability to balance business priorities, customer experience, delivery speed, technical quality, operational risk, and cost.
Excellent leadership, communication, stakeholder management, analytical, and decision-making skills.

About Pioneering Intelligence

Pioneering Intelligence builds on Flagship Pioneering's legacy of founding cutting-edge science and computational ventures, harnessing recent advances in AI, machine learning, and data to accelerate fundamental research and create a portfolio of AI-first companies. As part of Flagship's integrated model of science, entrepreneurship, and capital, it transforms breakthrough ideas into world-changing companies, elevating the AI advances happening across the ecosystem in human health, sustainability, and beyond.

The Role

The Pioneering Intelligence team at Flagship Pioneering builds the digital and AI foundation that accelerates the creation and growth of our companies. We are seeking a Vice President of Engineering to lead a medium sized team of Principal Software Engineers, each operating as the technical authority for their own product area.

This is a non-traditional engineering leadership role. Rather than managing a layered organization, you will build and support a team composed entirely of senior individual contributors operating as technical leads at the highest level. Each engineer owns end-to-end technical decisions, builds hands-on, and engages directly with scientific users. Your job is not to manage their work but to set the conditions in which exceptional engineers do their best work, remove obstacles, raise the collective bar, and translate technical strategy into organizational direction.

You remain technically active. You will contribute to architectural decisions, review complex system designs, and stay close enough to the work to lead credibly. You spend roughly 25% of your time in hands-on technical work. The rest is spent on strategy, people, and organizational leadership: building the team, aligning with product leadership, representing the function to senior stakeholders, and driving the conditions for fast, high-quality delivery across the portfolio.

The model is intentionally fluid. Principal Engineers on this team may move between pure IC work and the formal coordination of other resources as project needs evolve, including the management of fully embedded software engineering contractors. It is the VP who balances resources across all teams and projects, in close collaboration with product and strategy leads, ensuring the right people are working on the right things at the right time.

You will work in close partnership with product and strategy leads and alongside a team of peers who expect the same rigor and accountability from you that you expect from them.

Key Responsibilities

Lead and develop a team of approximately five Principal Software Engineers, each owning technical authority for their own product area
Set technical strategy and architectural direction for the AI and digital platform, making or ratifying the most consequential build-vs-buy and system design decisions
Stay technically active: contribute to architectural reviews, design complex systems, and maintain the credibility to lead a team of principal-level engineers
Build and maintain the team itself: hire exceptional engineers, develop their careers, and create a culture where the floor is principal-level performance
Represent engineering to product leadership, senior stakeholders, and across the Flagship ecosystem, translating technical direction into business impact
Balance resources across all teams and projects in close collaboration with product and strategy leads, including decisions about when Principal Engineers take on formal coordination of embedded SWE contractors versus pure IC work
Drive delivery across the portfolio by removing blockers, resolving cross-team dependencies, and ensuring the team ships with speed and quality
Model and advance an AI-native engineering culture, including the use of tools like Claude Code as organizational force multipliers

Experiences

Has led a team of senior individual contributors or principal-level engineers, ideally in a lean, high-velocity organization where the team was small and the scope was large
Has served as the technical authority on a complex, production-grade system, not as a manager who delegates the hard parts, but as an engineer who owned them
Has built and scaled engineering organizations in ambiguous, fast-moving environments, ideally at a startup or within a high-autonomy team inside a larger organization
Has worked closely with scientific or domain-expert users and understands how to build products that serve researchers, not just operators
Has hired and developed principal or staff-level engineers, with a track record of raising the technical bar of a team over time

Skills

Technically credible at the system design level: can evaluate architectural decisions, identify risk in complex designs, and contribute meaningfully to the hardest engineering conversations
Leads through clarity: sets direction, makes decisions, and communicates tradeoffs without requiring repeated alignment
Builds teams, not just products: knows how to hire exceptionally, develop senior talent, and create conditions where strong engineers stay and grow
Fluent in AI-native ways of working and comfortable leading a team that uses tools like Claude Code as a core part of their engineering practice
Writes with the same precision they expect from their engineers: strategy docs, architectural reviews, and hiring rubrics that don't require a follow-up meeting

Traits

Strategic and hands-on at the same time: comfortable moving between organizational leadership and technical depth without losing credibility in either

Founder-minded: attracted to ambiguity, motivated by impact, and able to build clarity from uncertainty rather than waiting for it to arrive

MongoDB is standing up a dedicated ISV Partnerships function, and this Director role is the leadership seat at the center of that effort. You will own the strategy and execution of MongoDB's ISV partner program across a team of partner managers, covering both industry-specific ISVs in verticals like financial services, healthcare, insurance, retail, and manufacturing, and horizontal AI-native ISVs building platforms and tools that serve builders across industries.

This is not a role for someone who wants to manage from a distance. You will set the strategic direction for how MongoDB identifies, activates, and scales ISV partnerships, while staying close enough to the work to directly influence key relationships, shape partner agreements, and coach your team through complex deals. You will be expected to operate as a player-coach: intellectually involved in the most important partnerships, hands-on when the moment calls for it, and consistently raising the bar for what good looks like on your team.

This is a greenfield program. You will have real ownership over how it is built, the methodology your team follows, how success is defined and measured, and how the function earns credibility with Sales, Product, and executive leadership. The opportunity is significant for the right leader.

This role can be based remotely in the United States.

What You'll Do

Strategy and Program Leadership

Define and own the strategic framework for MongoDB's ISV partner program, including segmentation across vertical and horizontal ISV categories, prioritization criteria, and the GTM approach for each partner tier
Build and evolve the program infrastructure: onboarding processes, partner playbooks, co-sell frameworks, success metrics, and the internal operating model that connects ISV partnerships to MongoDB's revenue motion
Set the vision for how ISV partnerships contribute to MongoDB's growth, and communicate that vision clearly to executive leadership, cross-functional stakeholders, and your team

Player-Coach Execution

Identify early signals of partnership potential or risk across your team's portfolio and step in directly when a deal or relationship needs senior attention
Model the behavior you expect from your team, including intellectual rigor in partner evaluation, commercial discipline in deal structuring, and a bias toward outcomes over activity

Team Development

Establish clear expectations for performance, build a culture of accountability, and create space for your team to do their best work without micromanagement
Contribute to future team hiring and organizational design as the ISV program scales

Cross-Functional Leadership

Build strong working relationships with Sales, Product, Marketing, and Pre-Sales leadership to align ISV partnership strategy with MongoDB's broader go-to-market priorities
Serve as the internal advocate for the ISV partner motion, educating field sellers on how to co-sell with ISV partners and working with Product to influence the roadmap based on partner ecosystem needs
Present program performance, strategic priorities, and resource needs to senior leadership on a regular basis

Ecosystem Positioning

Represent MongoDB externally at industry events, partner summits, and customer conversations to build visibility and accelerate business development

Developing and executing the North American IT strategy and multi-year technology roadmap.

We are seeking a Vice President of Engineering to lead a medium sized team of Principal Software Engineers, each operating as the technical authority for their own product area.

The model is intentionally fluid. Principal Engineers on this team may move between pure IC work and the formal coordination of other resources as project needs evolve, including the management of fully embedded software engineering contractors. It is the VP who balances resources across all teams and projects, in close collaboration with product and strategy leads, ensuring the right people are working on the right things at the right time.

You will need to be successful influencing cross-functionally across all levels of the organization, operating horizontally across multiple teams and pods, and drive clarity in ambiguous, complex technical domains. You must also be comfortable setting strategic direction while staying close enough to the work to make high-quality product and architecture decisions.

Define and drive the short- and long-term roadmap for Tanium’s end-to-end data architecture, including storage, access, query, visualization, and data movement capabilities.
Partner with Product Managers, Engineering, Design, and leadership across the organization to align priorities across multiple pods and ensure teams are building toward a cohesive data strategy.

new_jobs.description:
About The University

Manhattan University is nestled in the historic neighborhood or Riverdale , close to dozens of restaurants and shops as well as Van Cortlandt Park , and is only 35 minutes from midtown Manhattan. Manhattan University is nationally ranked and offers degree programs in the arts, business, education, engineering, and science. The University has approximately 2,900 full and part-time undergraduate and graduate students enrolled in over 50 fields of study. It is committed to excellence in teaching a diverse student body and preparing students for successful careers and fulfilling lives. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment where all employees and faculty members can thrive personally and professionally.

Position Description

The Director of Slate Technology and Data Analytics provides strategic and operational leadership for Manhattan University’s enrollment technology, data, analytics, and reporting ecosystem. Reporting to the Vice President for Enrollment Management and Marketing, the Director serves as the principal product owner and administrator for Technolutions Slate and translates institutional priorities into secure, efficient, student-centered processes that strengthen recruitment, admission, yield, enrollment, retention, and long-term financial sustainability.

The Director partners with Admissions, Marketing and Communications, Financial Aid, Jasper Central, Information Technology Services, Institutional Research and Assessment, Academic Affairs, Finance, faculty, and academic leadership to establish shared data definitions, improve cross-functional workflows, and deliver timely, actionable intelligence. The role advances Manhattan University’s transition from reactive operations to disciplined Strategic Enrollment Management through stronger CRM governance, automation, funnel analytics, forecasting, campaign attribution, and continuous improvement. The Director carries out this work in a manner consistent with the University’s person-centered Lasallian Catholic mission, respect for human dignity, ethical conduct, access, student success, and responsible stewardship of institutional resources.

Job Responsibilities

Slate Strategy, Administration, and Product Ownership

Serve as the primary Slate administrator and institutional product owner for enrollment-related functionality, with responsibility for platform strategy, governance, configuration, release management, testing, documentation, and continuous optimization.
Design and maintain applications, forms, portals, events, decision workflows, Reader processes, communications, permissions, rules, queues, scheduler functions, and other Slate capabilities supporting undergraduate, graduate, transfer, international, and continuing student populations.
Maintain a prioritized CRM roadmap aligned with the University’s Strategic Enrollment Management plan, enrollment targets, student-service standards, and available resources.
Establish development, testing, quality-assurance, deployment, change-control, and rollback practices that reduce operational risk and protect business continuity during critical recruitment and enrollment periods.
Monitor platform updates and emerging capabilities, including Slate AI, and recommend adoption only after evaluating business value, data readiness, privacy, accessibility, security, bias, accuracy, and appropriate human oversight.

Data Governance, Integration, Security, and Compliance

Lead enrollment data governance by establishing data definitions, ownership, quality standards, access controls, retention practices, and an authoritative source framework for key enrollment measures.
Build, monitor, document, and troubleshoot secure integrations among Slate, Ellucian Banner, financial aid systems, application services, marketing platforms, identity and access tools, Tableau or Power BI, and other approved University systems using APIs, web services, secure file transfer, SQL, and available middleware.
Conduct recurring audits of records, rules, imports, permissions, queries, reports, communications, and integrations; identify root causes and drive issues through documented resolution.
Apply role-based access and least-privilege principles, support single sign-on and multifactor authentication where applicable, and partner with Information Technology Services on incident response, risk assessment, vendor review, disaster recovery, and continuity planning.
Ensure adherence to FERPA, University privacy and security policies, records-retention requirements, accessibility standards, ethical recruitment practices, and applicable federal and state requirements.

Analytics, Forecasting, and Decision Support

Develop and maintain trusted dashboards, scorecards, recurring reports, and self-service tools that provide timely visibility into inquiry generation, applications, admits, deposits, melt, enrollment, retention, net tuition revenue, discounting, campaign performance, event conversion, engagement signals, and barriers to enrollment.
Provide weekly and cycle-based funnel reporting with year-over-year, goal, cohort, geography, program, source, and student-population comparisons; clearly identify risks, opportunities, and recommended actions.
Reconcile Slate recruitment, application, deposit, and enrollment reporting with Banner, payment systems, and official institutional reporting in partnership with Institutional Research, Finance, and relevant system owners. Document cohort definitions, reporting dates, status mappings, and historical snapshots, and explain material differences before reports are presented to leadership.
Support enrollment forecasting, scenario planning, predictive modeling, territory and market analysis, recruitment-source evaluation, and resource allocation for first-year, transfer, graduate, international, and other priority populations.
Develop measurement frameworks for communication and marketing effectiveness, including attribution, cost per inquiry or applicant, conversion, return on investment, and channel performance.
Present complex findings in concise, decision-ready formats for the President, Cabinet, Board committees, deans, and enrollment leadership while communicating limitations, assumptions, and data quality considerations.

Student Experience, Automation, and Operational Improvement

Use CRM design, automation, behavioral triggers, and workflow orchestration to reduce manual work, shorten response times, remove applicant friction, and deliver timely, personalized, accessible communications and next steps.
Partner with enrollment and academic teams to implement shared interaction logging, barrier-code triage, routing, escalation, and resolution tracking that support proactive outreach and coordinated service to students and families.
Continuously assess portals, forms, communications, checklists, event experiences, and decision processes for usability, clarity, mobile responsiveness, accessibility, and equitable outcomes.
Lead process mapping and redesign initiatives; establish service levels, operating procedures, controls, and documentation for high-volume and high-risk enrollment processes.

Leadership, Partnership, and Enablement

Serve as the principal liaison among Enrollment Management and Marketing, Admissions, Jasper Central, Information Technology Services, Institutional Research and Assessment, Financial Aid, Finance, Academic Affairs, and external technology partners.
Chair or facilitate a cross-functional Slate and enrollment-data governance group that prioritizes requests, resolves ownership questions, reviews change impacts, and monitors completion of approved initiatives.
Develop a community of practice for Slate users through role-based training, office hours, user guides, release notes, data dictionaries, and knowledge-transfer plans that reduce reliance on individual employees or consultants.
Manage assigned vendors, consultants, contracts, and project budgets; monitor deliverables, service quality, risk, and return on investment.
Supervise and develop assigned CRM, analytics, operations, student, or project staff, as applicable, and promote a culture of accountability, service, collaboration, innovation, and continuous improvement.

Other Duties

Lead special projects and provide strategic support to the President and the Vice President for Enrollment Management and Marketing as assigned to advance the goals of Manhattan University.
Responsibilities may evolve as institutional priorities, technology, regulations, and student needs change.

Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in information systems, data analytics, computer science, business, higher education, statistics, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and directly relevant experience.
Five or more years of progressively responsible experience administering Slate or a comparable enterprise CRM in higher education, including substantial experience with configuration, workflows, reporting, permissions, communications, integrations, and production support.
Demonstrated proficiency with SQL and relational data concepts; experience developing decision-ready dashboards and reports in Slate and a business-intelligence platform such as Tableau or Power BI.
Demonstrated experience integrating CRM, student information, financial aid, application, marketing, and analytics platforms through APIs, web services, secure file transfer, or middleware.
Strong knowledge of data governance, data quality, access management, privacy, information security, FERPA, documentation, testing, and change-control practices.
Ability to translate enrollment strategy and business needs into scalable technical solutions, manage competing priorities, lead projects to completion, and communicate effectively with technical and non-technical audiences.
Evidence of sound judgment, discretion, initiative, attention to detail, customer service, collaborative leadership, and commitment to ethical and responsible use of data and emerging technologies.
Strong appreciation for and ability to advance Manhattan University’s Lasallian Catholic mission and person-centered approach to education.

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in a relevant field.
Advanced Slate expertise across Deliver, Reader, portals, forms, events, Scheduler, query and report builders, configurable joins, rules, permissions, integrations, and Slate AI.
Experience with Ellucian Banner, Common Application and other application services, digital marketing and attribution platforms, student-success workflows, predictive analytics, and enterprise data visualization.
Experience supporting Strategic Enrollment Management across undergraduate, graduate, transfer, and international populations in a competitive, tuition-dependent, or urban private-university environment.
Experience leading CRM governance, data stewardship, process redesign, change management, vendor relationships, and staff development.
